hypothesis: After all on-board identities are public, the optimal continuation game graph is independent of unknown off-board capture identities. Canonicalizing their NNUE features may improve invariance and strength. Fixed opponent behavior can still depend on private history; this is not a universal policy-equivalence claim.

controls.A: original search/features and identically trained raw-data small NNUE
controls.B: canonical full-public NNUE features with A weights, without retraining
controls.C: canonical full-public features plus matched canonical-data training

native_change.change: Omit NNUE urn features only when both on-board dark counts are zero; force accumulator refresh on last-dark reveal/capture. Rules, actual position inventories, histories and chance search remain intact. This does not reveal or move a still-dark piece.

training_data.change: Only urn columns 91:103 set to zero when no on-board DARK remains. Original search-score and outcome labels, flags and all other fields unchanged.

validation_data.change: Only urn columns 91:103 set to zero when no on-board DARK remains. Original search-score and outcome labels, flags and all other fields unchanged.

scope: Single-seed development ablation, shared held-out initial layouts across arms; no promotion or pooled superiority claim. All original rule histories and inventory dynamics retained. No still-dark piece is replaced by its inferred revealed type.
